questions.stem: At pickup, a technician trainee encounters a patient question and an unresolved DUR alert. Which assignments comply with Massachusetts personnel rules? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Allow the trainee to counsel the patient independently.
Allow the trainee to resolve the DUR alert independently.
Treat trainee registration as pharmacist-intern licensure.
Limit the trainee to duties authorized for that category under pharmacist supervision.
Keep professional-judgment decisions with the pharmacist.

questions.stem: A pharmacy assigns support personnel to receive and process Schedule II stock. Which safeguards apply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Use only a personnel category authorized for the assigned step by 247 CMR 8.05.
Permit every technician trainee to receive Schedule II stock independently.
Maintain pharmacist supervision and pharmacist-only professional functions.
Allow a cashier to perform any handling step with manager approval.
Ignore personnel-scope rules because the product is Schedule II.

questions.stem: A pharmacy schedules an intern for a shift without a pharmacist preceptor directing the work. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A senior technician may serve as the preceptor.
The intern must work under direct supervision of a registered pharmacist preceptor.
Five hundred internship hours permit independent prescription verification.
Intern status does not authorize independent pharmacist practice.
The pharmacist preceptor remains responsible for the supervision relationship.

questions.stem: A student works a 14-hour pharmacy shift and asks to record every hour as internship credit. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: All 14 hours count because the student remained on site.
No more than 12 hours may be credited for that day.
The rule caps credit at eight hours per week.
Working additional hours does not increase the daily credit cap.
Only time handling controlled substances counts.

questions.stem: A pharmacist plans continuing education for the two-year Massachusetts renewal cycle. Which statements are generally correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Complete at least 20 contact hours in each calendar year.
Include at least two contact hours of pharmacy law each calendar year.
Use no more than 15 home-study hours in a calendar year absent an exception.
Carry unused hours freely into the next calendar year.
Do not carry unused annual hours into the next calendar year.

questions.stem: A pharmacist directly oversees both sterile and complex nonsterile compounding. Which continuing-education statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Meet the applicable annual sterile-compounding CE requirement.
Use general pharmacy-law CE in place of all compounding CE.
Also assess the annual complex-nonsterile compounding CE requirement.
Apply compounding CE only to technicians.
Treat the applicable requirements as cumulative when both activities are supervised.

questions.stem: A California prescriber issued an otherwise valid methylphenidate prescription six days ago. The patient presents it today at a Massachusetts pharmacy. Which threshold issue is dispositive?

choices.text: California is outside the narcotic contiguous-state list.
Methylphenidate becomes Schedule VI when issued outside Massachusetts.
The prescription is eligible because nonnarcotic Schedule II prescriptions have no timing gate.
The Massachusetts five-day presentation window has passed.

questions.stem: Which drug-status and Massachusetts legal-consequence pairings are accurate? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Pregabalin is Schedule V, and covered dispensing is MassPAT-reportable.
Gabapentin is federally noncontrolled but Massachusetts Schedule VI and MassPAT-reportable.
Methylphenidate is Schedule II and may not be refilled.
Pseudoephedrine is Schedule V because CMEA restricts retail sales.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a Focalin prescription issued four days ago by a properly registered New Hampshire prescriber. The pharmacist verifies the prescription and prescriber. Which conclusion is most defensible?

choices.text: Reject it because all out-of-state Schedule II prescriptions are prohibited.
Apply the five-day contiguous-state narcotic rule because all Schedule II drugs are narcotics.
Dispense under the nonnarcotic Schedule II out-of-state pathway after verification.
Use the 30-day out-of-state Schedule III-through-VI window.
Dispense without verification because New Hampshire is contiguous.

questions.stem: At same-day pickup, an opioid-naive adult receives a first outpatient methadone prescription for pain for 10 days with no documented exception. What should be clarified?

choices.text: Treat the prescription as exempt because methadone is always used for opioid dependence.
Apply only the general 30-day Schedule II opioid quantity ceiling.
Allow a 90-day fill because every methadone prescription qualifies for the OUD pathway.
Dispense ten days because the seven-day limit applies only to minors.
The prescriber must address the Massachusetts initial-opiate seven-day limit or document an applicable exception.

questions.stem: An adult receiving an outpatient opiate for acute pain for the first time presents an eight-day OxyContin prescription with no exception documentation. What is the key issue?

choices.text: The initial outpatient opiate supply is limited to seven days absent a documented statutory exception.
Dispense eight days because extended-release products are exempt.
Use the ordinary 30-day Schedule II opioid quantity limit without further inquiry.
Use the 90-day non-opioid Schedule II pathway.
Split the prescription into seven days now and one day as a refill.

questions.stem: During a profile review, a Norco prescription for a minor is written for 12 days, and the record sent with it contains no qualifying exception. What should the pharmacist recognize?

choices.text: Apply the seven-day restriction only if this is the minor's first opiate prescription.
A minor's opiate prescription is generally limited to seven days unless the prescriber documents a statutory exception.
Dispense 12 days if a parent signs at pickup.
Use the 30-day Schedule II ceiling because it displaces the minor-specific rule.
Accept the written 12-day quantity as the prescriber's implied exception.

questions.stem: At a Massachusetts pharmacy, a fentanyl prescription from a Rhode Island practitioner was issued four days ago and the pharmacist obtains direct verification. What Massachusetts rule is central?

choices.text: Use the 30-day out-of-state Schedule III-through-VI window.
Fill any state's Schedule II narcotic prescription within five days.
Skip direct verification because Rhode Island is contiguous.
Treat electronic transmission as resetting the five-day issue period.
Apply the contiguous-state Schedule II narcotic pathway and its five-day and verification conditions.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives an Ativan prescription issued 20 days ago by a properly authorized Connecticut practitioner. The pharmacist verifies the prescription and prescriber. What is the key determination?

choices.text: Reject it after five days under the Schedule II narcotic rule.
The prescription falls within the 30-day out-of-state Schedule IV pathway after verification.
Use the federal six-month clock as the only deadline.
Accept it without verification because Connecticut licenses the practitioner.
Require a Massachusetts prescriber for every Schedule IV prescription.

questions.stem: A patient presents an otherwise authentic out-of-state Ambien prescription 31 days after issue. What is the Massachusetts consequence?

choices.text: Fill it because federal Schedule IV authority lasts six months.
Use the five-day contiguous-state narcotic rule.
Accept the prescription after telephone verification on day 31.
The Massachusetts 30-day out-of-state window has expired.
Change the issue date to the date the pharmacy received it.

questions.stem: At a Massachusetts pharmacy, an adult's first outpatient tramadol prescription for acute pain requests a 10-day supply without exception documentation. What should be resolved?

choices.text: Apply only the five-refill and six-month Schedule IV limits.
Allow ten days because Schedule IV drugs are exempt from the opiate statute.
Reduce the quantity without contacting the prescriber and discard the balance.
Use the seven-day restriction only for patients younger than 18.
Resolve the Massachusetts initial-opiate seven-day limit before dispensing the requested quantity.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is evaluating eligibility to enter a collaborative practice agreement that includes prescribing. Which qualifications are required? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Hold a current unrestricted Massachusetts license, practice in the Commonwealth, and maintain the required $1,000,000 liability coverage.
Complete five years as a licensed pharmacist or satisfy the pre-July 2017 PharmD grandfather or a Board-equivalent education/residency pathway.
Devote practice to the defined therapy area and complete five additional related CE contact hours in each agreement year.
For prescriptive practice, maintain the required state controlled-substance registration, complete required training, and submit the MassHealth participation attestation.
A current PharmD alone satisfies the experience requirement regardless of when the agreement begins.

questions.stem: A retail collaborative program receives a physician referral for an adult patient who has not yet consented. Which limits apply before the pharmacist acts? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Obtain the required patient notice and consent.
Stay within the agreement, referral, authorized disease states, and retail scope.
Use the written agreement and supervising-physician framework.
Diagnose an unrelated disease independently.
Enroll any walk-in patient automatically.

questions.stem: A proposed retail collaborative agreement would let a pharmacist prescribe alprazolam and methylphenidate. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: $1,000,000 liability coverage waives the schedule restriction.
Only Schedule II prescribing is prohibited.
The agreement cannot authorize prescribing Schedule II through V drugs.
A supervising physician's signature does not remove that prohibition.
Schedule VI prescribing requires separate compliance with retail CDTM limits.

questions.stem: A retail collaborating pharmacist issues an authorized Schedule VI prescription for the patient's referred diagnosis. Which actions are required? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Add Schedule II refills under the same agreement.
Keep the prescription within the diagnosis and agreement scope.
Send a copy to the supervising physician within 24 hours.
Delay physician notice until the agreement is renewed.
Document the prescription in the patient's collaborative-practice record.

questions.stem: Prospective review identifies a clinically significant interaction before dispensing. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Ignore the alert because the prescription was electronically signed.
Delegate final resolution to a cashier.
Evaluate and resolve the issue before dispensing using professional judgment.
Dispense first and review the interaction next month.
Contact the prescriber or patient when needed to resolve the concern.

questions.stem: A pharmacy redesigns its patient-counseling workflow around a pickup signature. Which principles remain applicable? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Provide the meaningful counseling opportunity required by 247 CMR 9.18.
Treat every pickup signature as proof that counseling was adequate.
Delegate counseling to an unlicensed cashier.
Use pharmacist judgment and patient-specific information.
Omit counseling whenever a Medication Guide is supplied.

questions.stem: A Klonopin prescription states six refills, and the pharmacy has already dispensed five refills within five months. What should the pharmacist recognize about the requested sixth refill?

choices.text: Honor the sixth refill because it appears on the original.
Count only refills dispensed in Massachusetts.
Federal law limits Schedule IV prescriptions to five refills within six months, despite the prescriber's notation.
Allow another refill because five months is less than six months.
Convert the sixth refill into a partial fill of the fifth.

questions.stem: During prospective legal review, an unfilled electronic Librium prescription has already been transferred once at the patient's request. The patient now seeks a second transfer. What is the result?

choices.text: Permit a second transfer because no dose has been dispensed.
Print and fax it so the next transaction is no longer electronic.
Return it to the original pharmacy and treat that return as a refill.
Allow another transfer when the patient consents in writing.
Do not transfer it a second time under the federal one-time electronic controlled-prescription rule.

questions.stem: A Halcion prescription is five months old and has already been refilled five times. Which fact prevents another refill?

choices.text: Dispense because the six-month period remains open.
The five-refill maximum is exhausted even though the six-month period has not ended.
Treat five completed refills as five new prescriptions.
Add a refill after confirming stable therapy with the patient.
Apply the no-refill rule used for Schedule II drugs.

questions.stem: A patient requests transfer of an unfilled electronic Sonata prescription to a second DEA-registered retail pharmacy. Both pharmacists can communicate directly. What else must be confirmed?

choices.text: Confirm no prior transfer, preserve the electronic record, and verify state permission.
Transfer it even if the original prescription was paper.
Permit repeated transfers until the first dispensing.
Let a technician transmit the record without pharmacist communication.
Ignore Massachusetts transfer restrictions because federal permission preempts every state condition.

questions.stem: During an end-of-shift check, a pharmacy receives its first DEA registration and will begin stocking controlled substances tomorrow. What inventory event is required?

choices.text: Take the first inventory at the end of the first month.
Wait two years because only biennial inventories are required.
Inventory only Schedule II stock on the start date.
Take an initial inventory of controlled substances on the date controlled-substance activity begins.
Use the wholesaler's invoice as the pharmacy's initial inventory.

questions.stem: At a Massachusetts pharmacy, a pharmacy took its last complete controlled-substance inventory 25 months ago. What is the issue?

choices.text: No problem exists until 30 months have elapsed.
The annual pharmacy permit renewal resets the inventory clock.
Only Schedule II stock needs a biennial inventory.
A perpetual inventory removes the need for the biennial snapshot.
The federal biennial inventory interval has been exceeded.

questions.stem: A lower-priced product is reasonably available and appears on the Massachusetts interchangeable-drug list, but the prescriber marked a valid no-substitution direction. Which facts control? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Determine whether the no-substitution direction is valid.
Confirm that the proposed product is listed as interchangeable.
Substitute any drug in the same therapeutic class.
Confirm that the proposed product is reasonably available at a lower retail price.
Honor a valid prescriber direction against substitution.

questions.stem: A patient returns an unopened bottle that the pharmacy dispensed in error. Which actions are permitted or required? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Accept the medication under the dispensing-error return pathway.
Return the sealed bottle directly to saleable stock.
Quarantine it pending proper disposition.
Keep it out of saleable inventory.
Arrange proper disposal after quarantine.

FED-CIII-V-REFILL.title: Federal Schedule III and IV refill limits

authority.name: Federal Schedule III and IV refill limits

FED-CIII-V-REFILL.rule_summary: A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.

FED-CS-SCHEDULES.title: Federal controlled-substance schedules
FED-CS-SCHEDULES.rule_summary: Federal controlled-substance classifications are established in 21 CFR Part 1308; drug-specific questions must cite the exact applicable schedule section rather than an undifferentiated omnibus reference.

FED-EPCS-TRANSFER.title: One-time transfer of electronic controlled prescriptions

authority.name: One-time transfer of electronic controlled prescriptions

FED-EPCS-TRANSFER.rule_summary: At a patient's request, an unfilled electronic Schedule II through V prescription may be transferred once between DEA-registered retail pharmacies if allowed by state law, kept electronic, unaltered, and communicated directly between pharmacists.

FED-INVENTORY-BIENNIAL.title: Biennial controlled-substance inventory
FED-INVENTORY-BIENNIAL.rule_summary: After the initial inventory, a registrant must take a new controlled-substance inventory at least every two years. Current DEA regulation permits any date within two years of the previous biennial inventory; the related statutory general-physical-inventory language does not authorize delaying the DEA inventory beyond that regulatory two-year window.

FED-INVENTORY-INITIAL.title: Initial controlled-substance inventory
FED-INVENTORY-INITIAL.rule_summary: A registrant takes an initial controlled-substance inventory on the date it first engages in controlled-substance activity; if the registrant commences business with no controlled substances on hand, it must record that zero-stock fact as the initial inventory.

FED-PSE-QUANTITY.title: Federal pseudoephedrine retail quantity limits
FED-PSE-QUANTITY.rule_summary: For ordinary non-mail-order retail sales, federal CMEA rules limit pseudoephedrine base to 3.6 grams per purchaser per day and 9 grams per purchaser during a 30-day period.

MA-CDTM-CONTROLLED-LIMIT.title: Retail CDTM Schedule II through V prohibition

authority.name: Retail CDTM Schedule II through V prohibition

MA-CDTM-CONTROLLED-LIMIT.rule_summary: A retail collaborative practice agreement may not authorize the pharmacist to prescribe Schedule II through V controlled substances.

MA-CDTM-QUALIFICATIONS.title: Pharmacist qualifications for collaborative drug therapy management

authority.name: Pharmacist qualifications for collaborative drug therapy management

MA-CDTM-QUALIFICATIONS.rule_summary: A collaborating pharmacist must satisfy Massachusetts licensure, experience or degree, liability insurance, practice-focus, and additional annual continuing-education requirements.

MA-CDTM-RETAIL-SCOPE.title: Retail collaborative drug therapy management scope

authority.name: Retail collaborative drug therapy management scope

MA-CDTM-RETAIL-SCOPE.rule_summary: Retail CDTM is limited to referred and consenting adults, the diseases and actions authorized by statute, the supervising physician's agreement, and other statutory setting restrictions.

MA-CDTM-SVI-RX.title: Retail CDTM Schedule VI prescribing
MA-CDTM-SVI-RX.rule_summary: A properly authorized retail collaborating pharmacist may issue Schedule VI prescriptions for the referred diagnosis and must send a copy to the supervising physician within 24 hours.

MA-CE-COMPOUNDING.title: Massachusetts compounding continuing education
MA-CE-COMPOUNDING.rule_summary: A pharmacist overseeing or directly engaged in covered sterile or complex nonsterile compounding must complete the applicable additional annual compounding continuing-education hours.

MA-CII-OUTSTATE.title: Massachusetts dispensing of out-of-state Schedule II prescriptions
MA-CII-OUTSTATE.rule_summary: Massachusetts applies a five-day presentation window and different issuing-state conditions to out-of-state narcotic and nonnarcotic Schedule II prescriptions.

MA-COUNSELING.title: Massachusetts patient counseling
MA-COUNSELING.rule_summary: A pharmacist must comply with the patient-counseling requirements of 247 CMR 9.18, including a meaningful offer or provision in the settings and circumstances governed by the regulation.

MA-INTERCHANGE.title: Massachusetts interchangeable-drug dispensing
MA-INTERCHANGE.rule_summary: A pharmacist dispenses a less expensive reasonably available interchangeable product listed under Massachusetts standards unless the prescriber validly indicates no substitution or another exception applies.

MA-INTERN-12H.title: Daily pharmacy internship credit limit
MA-INTERN-12H.rule_summary: A pharmacy intern may receive no more than 12 hours of pharmacy internship credit in one day.

MA-INTERN-SUPERVISION.title: Direct supervision of Massachusetts pharmacy interns

authority.name: Direct supervision of Massachusetts pharmacy interns

MA-INTERN-SUPERVISION.rule_summary: A Massachusetts pharmacy intern works under the direct supervision of a registered pharmacist preceptor.

MA-OPIOID-SEVEN-DAY.title: Massachusetts initial opioid seven-day limit
MA-OPIOID-SEVEN-DAY.rule_summary: An initial outpatient opiate prescription for an adult and any opiate prescription for a minor is generally limited to seven days, subject to documented statutory exceptions; opioid-dependence treatment is excluded.

MA-OUTSTATE-CII-NARCOTIC.title: Out-of-state Schedule II narcotic prescriptions
MA-OUTSTATE-CII-NARCOTIC.rule_summary: Massachusetts may fill a Schedule II narcotic prescription from Maine or a contiguous state within five days of issue after required authentication and verification; separate delivery provisions govern certain out-of-state residents.

MA-PHARMACIST-CE.title: Massachusetts pharmacist continuing education
MA-PHARMACIST-CE.rule_summary: A renewing pharmacist generally completes 20 contact hours in each calendar year of the two-year cycle, including at least two hours of pharmacy law each year, with limits on home study and daily credit.

MA-PMP-REPORTING.title: Massachusetts pharmacy MassPAT dispensing-data reporting

authority.name: Massachusetts PMP Data Submission Guide for Dispensers

MA-PMP-REPORTING.rule_summary: Covered pharmacies report dispensing of Schedule II through V controlled substances and DPH-designated additional drugs, including gabapentin, to the Massachusetts PMP under the current submission standard.

MA-PRODUR.title: Prospective drug utilization review
MA-PRODUR.rule_summary: Before dispensing, a pharmacist must perform the prospective drug utilization review required by 247 CMR 9.17 and resolve clinically significant issues through professional judgment and communication.

MA-RETURN-QUARANTINE.title: Returned erroneous or defective medication quarantine

authority.name: Returned erroneous or defective medication quarantine

MA-RETURN-QUARANTINE.rule_summary: A pharmacy accepts medication it dispensed in error or that is suspected defective or contaminated, but may not return it to inventory and must quarantine and properly dispose of it.

MA-RX-CV-REFILL.title: Massachusetts Schedule V prescription refill limits
MA-RX-CV-REFILL.rule_summary: A Massachusetts Schedule V prescription may not be refilled more than five times or later than six months after the prescription was issued.

MA-RX-OUTSTATE-III-VI.title: Out-of-state Schedule III through VI prescriptions

authority.name: Out-of-state Schedule III through VI prescriptions

MA-RX-OUTSTATE-III-VI.rule_summary: An authorized out-of-state practitioner may issue a Schedule III through VI prescription filled in Massachusetts within 30 days of issue; Schedule III through V prescriptions require pharmacist verification.

MA-TECH-CII.title: Schedule II handling by pharmacy support personnel

authority.name: Schedule II handling by pharmacy support personnel

MA-TECH-CII.rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 8.05, a pharmacy intern may handle Schedule II controlled substances under direct pharmacist supervision; an ordinary pharmacy technician may assist with transporting Schedule II substances, while a certified pharmacy technician may assist with transporting and handling them when the pharmacist supervises and approves the activity and written policies and procedures govern it. Pharmacist professional judgment is not delegated.

MA-TECH-SCOPE.title: Massachusetts pharmacy technician scope and pharmacist responsibility

authority.name: Massachusetts pharmacy technician scope and pharmacist responsibility

MA-TECH-SCOPE.rule_summary: Pharmacy technicians and trainees may perform only duties allowed by 247 CMR 8 under pharmacist supervision; judgmental pharmacist functions may not be delegated.
